owner.label: Owns
owner.note: This system does the work and is accountable for the outcome

required.label: Must change
required.note: Cannot be achieved without a change in this system

consumer.label: Consumes
consumer.note: Affected by the outcome but requires no change

milestones.name: Where we actually started
milestones.summary: 10 realised trades, all losers. Expectancy −367 CAD/trade, lifetime −15,935 CAD. The live map held one strategy that emitted zero signals when computed honestly. Honest valuation as a trading business: ~$0.
milestones.plain: The baseline, written down without flattery. Ten real trades, ten losses, and the one strategy that was live turned out to be running on a bug.

milestones.name: Honest zero
milestones.summary: Nothing in the live map that cannot fire in real time. `Range_Stochastic_Divergence` struck off via `INTEGRITY_DISQUALIFIED`; regimes re-fit with corrected label ordering and causal smoothing (kappa ≥ 0.83); finding B re-tested against honest labels and it stands.
milestones.plain: The measured value stayed at zero — but it became a true zero. Every measurement taken after this point can be trusted, which is the only reason the rungs above it mean anything.
milestones.falsifier: If the map still routes to a strategy whose honest signal count is zero, M1 is not met regardless of what else was built.

milestones.name: First honest qualifier
milestones.summary: Three cells now sit in the live map as `qualified` — but only after the OOS gate was lowered from 60 months to 12 on 2026-08-21, and they rest on 5, 13 and 20 out-of-sample trades. Their profit factors (6.8–13.6) and drawdowns (0.02%–1%) are small-sample artefacts, stated as such by the owner. Measured against the original gates, the strongest honest candidate remains `demark_fractal_breakout` USD_JPY H4: 610 OOS trades, PF 1.51, Sharpe 1.11 — one passing cell in roughly 230.
milestones.plain: On paper, three strategies passed. In practice they passed because the bar was lowered and because nothing checks how many trades the evidence contains — five trades is not a track record. The one result that would genuinely count has 610 trades behind it and works on a single currency pair.
milestones.falsifier: A qualifier that would not survive re-imposing the 60-month gate and a minimum trade count is not a qualifier; it is a sample-size artefact.

milestones.name: Forward test
milestones.summary: A signal travels the full three-system path on the practice account and its realised results track expectation. The drill design is specified: System 1 publishes one correctly-formed signal carrying `"drill": true`, System 3 processes it through the full risk path with the flag intact, System 2 runs it to the broker call and stops, logging the order it would have sent.
milestones.plain: Prove the pipe before trusting it with anything. One clearly-marked test order is sent down the whole chain; the last machine stops just short of actually placing it and writes down exactly what it would have done.
milestones.falsifier: If the same `signal_id` is not visible at all three systems, the pipe is not proven, however healthy each machine looks on its own.

milestones.name: Verified track record
milestones.summary: A continuous, auditable, out-of-sample equity curve of sufficient length to underwrite. This is the asset. Everything before it is infrastructure.
milestones.plain: A long enough run of honest results that somebody else would take it seriously. Buyers underwrite an equity curve first and inspect the engineering second.
milestones.falsifier: A curve with a gap, a restatement, or an unexplained parameter change in the middle is not a track record.

goals.title: Prove the signal pipe end to end across all three computers

metric.name: Links verified
metric.note: Link 1 (System 1 publish) is the only leg with any positive evidence. Links 2 and 3 are now negatively confirmed, not merely unverified — see dependencies.

goals.why: Signals route `S1 → Scored_Signal_Queue → S3 → AMS_Outbound_Queue → S2`. System 1 publishes to link 1 and that is verified. Links 2 and 3 are unverified and System 1 is blind to them — its service account is publisher-only and cannot list topics or subscriptions. Nothing else about model quality can matter until a message is observed arriving.
goals.plain: Three machines, two pipes between them. We can prove letters are going into the first pipe. Nobody has yet confirmed in writing that anyone is collecting them, or where the reply goes.
goals.definition_of_done: A written reply from System 3 naming its subscription on `Scored_Signal_Queue`, confirming a consumer is actually pulling it, and naming the topic it publishes approved orders to. Not 'it should be set up'. Then the same `signal_id` observed at all three systems during the drill.

dependencies.need: Publish; raise producer cadence to at least hourly during market hours

Per System 2's own trace (2026-08-27): the execution engine stopped 2026-08-24T17:07:55Z alongside System 3's gate, no restart since, no exception logged. Its only runtime window this week (10:52-17:07 Monday) shows no order or fill events at all — zero OANDA fills, confirmed operational rather than risk-gate related. Supersedes the 2026-08-22 note about the local-queue path; the process is not running at all now, so that misconfiguration is moot until it restarts.

Per System 3's own trace (2026-08-27): `ams.service.main` stopped simultaneously with System 2 at 2026-08-24T17:07:53Z, never restarted. Separately and independently of the outage: System 3 has never had a real Pub/Sub consumer running — `pubsub_signal_relay.py` has no systemd unit and no log evidence it has ever executed. `ams_decision_log` holds one entry since 2026-08-23 (Sunday's drill) and zero for Mon/Tue/Wed; none of System 1's 46 real signals this week reached System 3. Supersedes the 2026-08-22 claim of an active relay pulling 13,020 times/24h — that claim does not hold up against the decision log.

goals.title: Raise the producer cadence to at least hourly

metric.name: Producer runs per trading day
metric.note: Confirmed via `crontab -l` and a full week of `logs/cron_hourly_signals.log` (2026-08-24 through 2026-08-27): hourly cron at :15, 24 runs/day.

goals.why: The producer fires from `cron_daily_ingest_and_signals.sh` at 22:30 on weekdays. Two of the three live strategies are H4 — six bars a day — so a once-daily batch emits signals for bars that closed up to twenty hours earlier. `src/signals/run.py` already supports a continuous 60-second loop.
goals.plain: Trade ideas are posted once a night, but most of the strategies produce a new idea every four hours. Almost everything posted is describing a moment that has already gone.
goals.definition_of_done: `crontab -l` shows the producer running at least hourly during market hours. Recommendation on record: hourly cron before continuous service — smaller change, restartable, matches the existing operational pattern.

dependencies.need: Done 2026-08-2x: hourly cron installed (`shell/cron_hourly_signals.sh`, :15 past every hour). Verified against a full week of logs — 46 real signals published Mon-Wed, 0 dead-lettered.

Cadence is not cosmetic for us: the `ScoredSignal` TTL is 15 minutes. A once-daily 22:30 batch produces signals that are hours past that TTL on arrival, so they are discarded before any risk logic runs. Hourly is the minimum at which H4 signals survive the trip.

goals.title: Resolve ADR-001 — decide where live inference runs
goals.why: Two incompatible architectures are on record. The code makes trading depend on Computer 1 — a host with unreliable networking — so if that machine is offline, nothing trades anywhere. That coupling is in no design document and is the direct cause of the incident in which the producer had never emitted a message and nobody could see why.
goals.plain: The whole operation currently depends on the least reliable computer in the building being awake. The proposal is to move the live work onto the machine that is already awake during market hours, and let the research machine go back to sleep.
goals.definition_of_done: System 2 and System 3 each reply APPROVE or REJECT with reasons, against their actual implementations rather than against the document. No implementation starts before both approve.

dependencies.need: Authored the ADR; would decommission its producer in the same change that enables System 2 inference

Reviewed 2026-08-22 — **approve with conditions**. Would run inference; already runs verified artifact sync and live HMM inference. Conditions: prove the transport first, sign the manifest rather than only checksumming it, run bundle strategy code in a least-privilege process with no broker credential, and gate cutover on a determinism test against System 1's own outputs.

Reviewed 2026-08-22 — **approve with conditions**. Responsibilities are unchanged and the publisher's identity is irrelevant to the gate. The envelope is not: it needs a required `producer`, a `bundle_id`, and a `drill` boolean, and that change must land before System 2 starts publishing, not after.

goals.title: Add a minimum trade-count gate to vetting

metric.name: Live cells below a defensible sample size

goals.why: `vet.py` treats `trade_count` only as a ranking tie-break, so there has never been a rule about how much evidence a qualification rests on. Combined with the 2026-08-21 reduction of `oos_months` from 60 to 12, cells with 5, 13 and 20 trades reached the live map with profit factors of 6.8 to 13.6.
goals.plain: Nothing in the examiner checks how many trades a strategy's track record actually contains. A strategy with five trades can therefore score spectacularly and be waved through — but five trades is noise.
goals.definition_of_done: A minimum trade-count gate exists in `gates.py` with a stated threshold and a test, and no cell below it can appear in a published map. Worth adding regardless of where the `oos_months` value finally lands.

dependencies.need: Implement the gate and re-run vetting

Sizing is derived from the measured edge, so a thin cell produces an unreliable Kelly fraction. In practice the sizing layer already refuses on insufficient or stale live statistics — 1,100 of 4,091 rejections to date — so the protection exists, but it arrives as a refusal to size rather than as a refusal to qualify.

goals.title: Fix qualified strategies published with empty exits
goals.why: All three entries in the current live map carry `exits: {}`. A strategy with no exit specification serializes cleanly and passes every schema check, but means nothing to whoever has to execute it — the executing system has been told when to enter and never told when to leave.
goals.plain: Every strategy currently live says how to open a trade and says nothing at all about how to close one. It looks perfectly valid to every automated check on the way out.
goals.definition_of_done: `vet.py` refuses to publish a cell with an empty `exits` object, with a guarding test. The three live entries either gain exits or leave the map.

dependencies.need: Fix the defect in `vet.py`
Position management executes exit parameters carried on the order; with none supplied there is nothing to execute, and trailing stops and time-based exits are inert.

Layer `H` compares the maximum hold duration against the next Friday cutoff. With `exits: {}` it falls back to the configured maximum rather than the strategy's own — 131 rejections have already landed there.

goals.title: Stand up the System 3 AMS schema and service skeleton
goals.why: System 3's design is ratified but nothing runs on Computer 3. Its own PostgreSQL is a hard requirement, not a convenience — the guardian must keep operating when Computer 1 is asleep, which is its normal state.
goals.plain: The risk officer exists on paper only. Its checkpoints, its memory of the account, and its ability to say no all still need building.
goals.definition_of_done: Local PostgreSQL provisioned on Computer 3; account state machine persisted; gate layers A–J implemented with per-layer reason codes; median decision latency measured under 100 ms.

dependencies.need: Retrain triggers will eventually read decay signals from here

The 30-second account snapshot **is** serving, so layers A–C are not inert. It is produced by `s2s3-bridge.service` rather than by System 2 itself: System 2's built EXEC tasks contain no snapshot producer, and the bridge reads System 2's credential so System 3 still never sees the broker key.

Largely built and running, not planned: 13 gate layers with per-layer reason codes, a persisted state machine, and 4,153 logged decisions at 0.75 ms mean latency. This goal's metric reads 0 of 10 layers implemented; 13 are implemented. What genuinely remains is the datastore — it is SQLite, and local PostgreSQL has never been provisioned.

goals.title: Close the look-ahead defect class across the research fleet
goals.why: `detect_swing_points` used a centred window and contaminated 36 of the 51 research strategies plus the only live strategy at the time. This is not one bug; it is a category of bug that makes losing systems look profitable, and it must be closed by an automated check rather than by review.
goals.plain: A helper was letting strategies peek at tomorrow's prices. Any result built on it was worthless. The fix is not to check each strategy by hand — it is to make it impossible to ship one that peeks.
goals.definition_of_done: Every strategy in the fleet passes `assert_no_lookahead_v2` in CI, and no measurement is published for a strategy that has not.

dependencies.need: Fix the centred-window usages and gate the harness on the assertion

goals.title: Reach M3 — a drill signal visible at all three systems
goals.why: Every proposal should answer one question: which rung of the ladder does this move? Work that moves no rung is a cost, however good the engineering. M1 is reached, M2 is contested, M3 is the next honest rung.
goals.plain: A single test for whether a piece of work is worth doing: does it move the project closer to a real, provable track record? If not, it waits.
goals.definition_of_done: One signal carrying `"drill": true` is published by System 1, processed by System 3 through the full risk path with the flag intact, and run by System 2 to the broker call and no further — with the logged order matching what System 1 sent, and the same `signal_id` visible at all three.

dependencies.need: Publish the drill signal at a realistic live price

Can already stop at the broker call — `EXEC_SHADOW=true` constructs the order and does not submit — and log what it would have sent. **Blocked** on the flag never reaching it: both System 3 contracts are `additionalProperties: false`.

**Blocked.** `ScoredSignal.schema.json` is `additionalProperties: false`, so a signal carrying `"drill": true` fails validation at the relay, which by design never acks an invalid message — System 1 would publish and hear nothing back, ever. `ApprovedOrder.schema.json` has the same setting, so the flag could not be forwarded either. Contract change first, drill second.

tasks.title: Raise the producer to at least hourly during market hours
tasks.detail: Owner decision needed: hourly cron or continuous service. Hourly cron recommended — smaller change, restartable, matches the existing pattern.

tasks.title: FIX-S1-016 — repair the signal producer
tasks.detail: It checked publication status on the wrong artifact, a condition nothing could satisfy, and crashed on import because the causal routing label had been deleted with a retired experiment. Both fixed, verified end to end against the live GCS bundle.

tasks.title: Switch QUEUE_PROVIDER from local to pubsub
tasks.detail: Signals had been landing in a directory on Computer 1 that no other machine could ever read.

tasks.title: Publish the drill signal
tasks.detail: One correctly-formed signal on a real instrument at a realistic live price, carrying "drill": true. Runs after links 2 and 3 are confirmed.

tasks.title: Add a minimum trade-count gate to gates.py
tasks.detail: With a stated threshold and a guarding test. Revisit after the pipe is proven.

tasks.title: Refuse to publish cells with empty exits
tasks.detail: All three live entries currently carry exits: {}.

tasks.title: Close the test-fixture leak into the production queue
tasks.detail: A test run once wrote fixtures into the live queue artefact — the entry: 1.05 messages System 2 saw. Not blocking, not closed.

tasks.title: Await APPROVE/REJECT on ADR-001 from Systems 2 and 3
tasks.detail: No implementation starts before both reply. Until then the producer is a bridge, not the destination.

tasks.title: Gate the research harness on assert_no_lookahead_v2
tasks.detail: Make it impossible to publish a measurement for a strategy that has not passed the assertion.

tasks.title: Wrap persist_trade_outcomes in a transaction
tasks.detail: Currently DELETE-then-rebuild with no transaction, and the default --lookback-years 5 silently discards half the history.

tasks.title: State which topic and subscription System 2 consumes
tasks.detail: Answered in full. Consumes the local subscription `ams-outbound.executor` and publishes to `ams-inbound` / `ams-inbound.ams`, all topics in a shared SQLite queue under `QUEUE_PROVIDER=local`. It has never consumed from Pub/Sub: `AMS_Outbound_Queue_sub` has no `pull_request_count` time series at all over seven days. So yes — the whole order path is a file-based queue, and it can never receive anything System 1 publishes to Pub/Sub.
tasks.evidence: `gcloud pubsub subscriptions list`; Cloud Monitoring `subscription/pull_request_count`, 7 d; deployed `config/.env.system2`

tasks.title: Add alarming on a silent inbound queue
tasks.detail: Partly built and demonstrably insufficient. EXEC-008 pauses at queue age over 300 s in-session, and `ops-watchdog.timer` pages Telegram every 30 minutes on a composite *running but not trading* condition — but that composite needs at least 8 gate decisions in a 3-hour window before *all rejected* means anything, which never happens when nothing arrives at all. Two days of a stranded queue produced no page. Missing rule: lifetime `messages_seen == 0` while queue depth is non-zero is broken, not quiet.

tasks.title: Run the drill signal to the broker call and stop
tasks.detail: The stopping half is ready — `EXEC_SHADOW=true` already constructs the order and does not submit, and the practice endpoint is confirmed (`OANDA_ENV=practice`, account `101-002-38449021-001`). Blocked because the flag cannot arrive: System 3's `ScoredSignal` and `ApprovedOrder` schemas are both `additionalProperties: false`. Unblocked by T-308.

tasks.title: Review ADR-001 and reply APPROVE or REJECT
tasks.detail: Approve with conditions, recorded in `decisions.json`. Candle warm-up is a config change — no local candle store exists, `OandaCandleSource` fetches on demand and 252 D1 bars is well within OANDA's per-request limit. Price agreement with System 1 is **unverified** and not claimed; see T-208. Executing System-1-authored code is acceptable given a signed manifest, a pinned and hashed dependency set, and a least-privilege process holding no broker credential.

tasks.title: Serve the 30-second account snapshot API
tasks.detail: Serving, and reconciled 2,601 times with the most recent snapshot 29 s old at the time of writing. Produced by `s2s3-bridge.service` rather than System 2 itself, because System 2's built EXEC tasks contain no snapshot producer; the bridge reads System 2's credential, so System 3 still never sees the broker key. A missing snapshot resolves to REJECT at layer `S`, not to a stale value.

tasks.title: Repair the queue binding and assert it at startup
tasks.detail: The deployed `.env.system2` sets `QUEUE_LOCAL_PATH` to a Windows absolute path; on the Linux host that is a filename, so System 2 opened an empty database beside its own source tree while System 3 and the bridge use `/opt/scalablebrain/shared/queue/queue.db`. Two parts: correct the value, and make `build_queue()` refuse to start unless the resolved path is absolute and already exists. A queue that silently creates itself when misconfigured is how two systems end up on two queues twice.

tasks.title: Reload the regime bundle after an artifact swap
tasks.detail: `LiveRegimeDetector.load_bundle` returns early while a bundle is cached and nothing calls it with `force=True`, so the model set is pinned at process start. Inference is running against `2026-08-17T09-28-46Z-d593220a` while `active` points at `2026-08-21T16-29-15Z-372f6956`. Also report the id actually in use on `/status`, rather than the downloader's — the divergence is currently invisible.

tasks.title: Reconcile our candles against System 1's, bar for bar
tasks.detail: We read OANDA mid candles (`price=M`, completed only) on demand and keep no local store; System 1's ingest is recorded as MBA. Nobody has compared a bar. ADR-001 makes this load-bearing: a regime label computed from a different price series is a different label. Compare a fixed window on D1, H4 and H1 across the live instruments and record the maximum discrepancy.

tasks.title: Correct the operational claims that are wrong at source
tasks.detail: Two documentation defects that would mislead an operator under pressure. The `downloader.py` docstring says the poll is ~15 min; it is 300 s. And any runbook naming SIGUSR1 as the emergency stop is wrong — SIGUSR1 appears nowhere in the codebase; STOP is SIGTERM/SIGINT, an in-process `trigger()`, or `touch state/control/STOP`. Sending SIGUSR1 in an emergency would do nothing at all.

tasks.title: Clear the standing false-positive watchdog alert
tasks.detail: `watchdog_state.json` has carried the episode `s2:producer` — *signal producer running=false* — open since 2026-08-15T18:09:26Z. That became correct behaviour the day local signal production was removed. A permanently-lit alert trains the operator to ignore the one channel that is meant to carry the real one.

tasks.title: Plan the three-process Pub/Sub cutover as one change
tasks.detail: `build_queue()` returns a single backend for every topic, so flipping one process moves both its legs and disconnects the other two. System 2, System 3 and the bridge must move together, and the relay is deleted in the same change. Runs after T-206 and after one message has been observed travelling the whole path on the current transport.

tasks.title: Name the subscription on Scored_Signal_Queue in writing
tasks.detail: Answered with evidence. Subscription `scored_signal_queue_sub`, topic `scored_signal_queue`, both lowercase — `Scored_Signal_Queue` has never existed in the project. A consumer is pulling right now: `s3-signal-relay.service`, up since 2026-08-17, 13,020 successful pull requests in the last 24 hours and 55,347 over seven days. Approved orders are published to `ams-outbound`, bridged onto `ams-outbound.executor`.

tasks.title: Provision local PostgreSQL on Computer 3
tasks.detail: Honest answer: no, and there is no Computer 3 to provision it on. System 3 runs on the shared VM `trading-1` with `DB_PROVIDER=sqlite`, `DB_PATH=state/db/ams.db`. The host's `postgresql@18-main` cluster serves System 2's database only. Postgres is supported and the migrations exist; SQLite has carried 4,153 decisions without loss, so this is a scale and concurrency concern rather than a correctness one today.
tasks.evidence: deployed `config/.env.system3`; `SELECT datname FROM pg_database` returns only `postgres` and `system2`

tasks.title: Implement the account state machine with persistence
tasks.detail: Built and running. DEMO → ACTIVE → CAUTION → PAUSED → CIRCUIT_BROKEN → RECOVERY, persisted in `ams_account_state` and written before any approval is published. Currently RECOVERY at stage `paper`, 4.85% below an 88,294.53 equity peak.

tasks.title: Implement gate layers A–J with per-layer reason codes
tasks.detail: All ten exist, plus three the design never had: `P` provenance, `Q` quarantine and `S` account-truth freshness. Built order is P, Q, A, S, B–G, sizing, H, I, J — and the letters do not match the earlier description: `H` is the Friday-cutoff duration check, `I` is the calendar, `J` is final sanity and assembly, and sizing is a separate step between `G` and `H`. Every rejection records its layer and reason. 4,153 decisions logged at 0.75 ms mean, 421 ms max.

tasks.title: Review ADR-001 and reply APPROVE or REJECT
tasks.detail: Approve with conditions, recorded in `decisions.json`. Yes, the envelope must change — a required `producer`, a `bundle_id`, and a `drill` boolean — and it must change before System 2 starts publishing, because `additionalProperties: false` means any new field is dead-lettered rather than ignored. The duplicate-publisher hazard needs the producer field to be required so an unexpected producer can be rejected outright.

tasks.title: Process the drill signal with the flag intact
tasks.detail: Cannot run. `ScoredSignal.schema.json` is `additionalProperties: false`, so a signal carrying `"drill": true` fails validation at the relay — which by design never acks and never forwards an invalid message, so it retries and dead-letters and System 1 hears nothing back. `ApprovedOrder.schema.json` is the same, so the flag could not be forwarded to System 2 either. Layer `P` adds a second trap: `selection_basis` must be present or the signal is rejected outright. Unblocked by T-308.

tasks.title: Build the post-trade journal and decay auditor
tasks.detail: Built. `trade_journal` and `daily_summary` persist realised trades, `audit/auditor.py` runs the decay bench, and quarantined strategies are refused at layer `Q`. Deliberately narrow — the only thing that leaves is a quarantine verdict. It is not yet exported anywhere System 1 can read it; that is T-311.

tasks.title: Add producer, bundle id and drill to the contracts
tasks.detail: Blocking G-008 and blocking ADR-001's transition. `ScoredSignal.schema.json` gains a **required** `producer`, a `bundle_id` and an optional `drill` boolean; `ApprovedOrder.schema.json` gains `drill` so the flag survives our egress. `producer` is required rather than optional so an unexpected publisher can be rejected outright during the transition, which is the only thing that catches two producers emitting different `signal_id`s for the same bar. Publish the updated contracts to `gs://scalable-brain-artifacts/contracts/v1/`.

tasks.title: Fix single-channel alerting
tasks.detail: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_USER` and `SMTP_TO` are blank in the deployed environment, so the urgency-routed email fallback described in the design does not exist. Every alert this system can raise depends on one Telegram bot token. Either configure the fallback or record an explicit decision to accept a single channel — but a design that claims two and ships one is the worse of the three options.

tasks.title: Inspect and drain the dead-letter queues
tasks.detail: `scored-signals.ams.dlq` holds 9 messages and `ams-inbound.ams.dlq` holds 532. They are visible by design rather than dropped, but nothing routinely reads them and a DLQ nobody reads is a discard with extra steps. Classify what is in them, then report DLQ depth on `/health` so it has an owner.

tasks.title: Export decay and quarantine verdicts where System 1 can read them
tasks.detail: The auditor and layer `Q` work locally, so a decayed strategy is refused here but System 1 is never told. Publish quarantine verdicts to GCS on the same read-only basis as everything else that crosses between systems. Keep it narrow — a verdict and its evidence, not live performance data, so the research side cannot start fitting to recent luck.

tasks.title: Audit signal cadence and queue backlog for the week of 2026-08-24
tasks.detail: Producer confirmed hourly and healthy: 46 real signals published (5 Mon, 9 Tue, 10 Wed, quiet Thu — normal for strategies that fire ~3x/week/pair), 0 dead-lettered. Checked `scored_signal_queue_sub` backlog directly with a personal gcloud identity (non-destructive, no --auto-ack): it holds exactly one message, a stray 2026-08-23 drill signal, not any of this week's real ones — evidence something is consuming, not proof of a fill. Still unconfirmed: whether System 2's local-queue misconfiguration (T-206, recorded 2026-08-22, status not_started as of that snapshot) has been fixed since. If not, that alone explains signals flowing with nothing trading.
tasks.evidence: logs/cron_hourly_signals.log; results/state/signal_emitter_state.json; `gcloud pubsub subscriptions pull scored_signal_queue_sub --project=scalable-brain --limit=10` (no --auto-ack)

tasks.title: Resolve the Pub/Sub backlog-vs-decision-log discrepancy
tasks.detail: System 1's non-destructive check of `scored_signal_queue_sub` (2026-08-27) found this week's 46 real signals absent from the backlog. System 2/3's own trace of `ams_decision_log` the same day found zero decisions for Mon/Tue/Wed and no evidence the relay script has ever run. Both cannot be fully explained together yet. Narrowed so far: the subscription's IAM policy grants pubsub.subscriber to exactly one identity, `trading-vm@scalable-brain.iam.gserviceaccount.com`; Data Access audit logs are not enabled for Pub/Sub in this project, so the actual consuming caller and timestamp cannot be recovered retroactively. Ruled out: this machine's own two peek pulls this session (both non-acking, and the backlog was already down to one message on the very first pull). Next step: enable Pub/Sub Data Access audit logging, then re-run the producer and watch who acks in real time.
tasks.evidence: gcloud pubsub subscriptions get-iam-policy scored_signal_queue_sub; gcloud logging read (Data Access logs absent); ams_decision_log query (System 2/3 side)
